items.title: South Africans vote in municipal elections seen as test for ANC
items.why: Polls opened at 7am on Wednesday across South Africa for elections to 257 councils, including Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban. A record 29.2 million people are registered, the electoral commission says, and 1.4 million special votes were cast on Monday and Tuesday. Final results are expected on Sunday.
items.matters: Polls suggest the ANC, which lost its national majority in 2024, could fall below 40%, Al Jazeera reports.

items.title: Democrats win control of both houses of US Congress in midterms
items.why: Democrats won control of the US Senate and House in Tuesday's midterm elections, AP and US networks project, flipping at least seven Republican Senate seats, including Texas, Ohio and Maine. Senate races in Alaska and Nebraska and many House seats, including in California, are still being counted.
items.matters: President Trump has threatened to veto Democratic bills. Democrats also flipped governorships in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Iowa.

items.title: Asian tech shares fall as Democrats win control of US Congress
items.why: Japan's Nikkei closed 1.4% lower on Wednesday after falling more than 4% during the day, with chip and AI firms such as SoftBank, Advantest and Kioxia hit hardest, AFP and CNBC report. US stock futures and the dollar also fell.
items.matters: JPMorgan analysts warned of an AI sell-off if investors expect tighter rules on data centres and tech under a Democratic Congress.

items.title: PSG beat Villarreal 6-0; Manchester United come back to beat Roma
items.why: In Tuesday's Champions League games, Paris Saint-Germain won 6-0 at Villarreal in Spain, scoring four in 17 minutes, which UEFA called the fastest four in the competition. Manchester United came from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2, Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0 and Bayern Munich won 2-0 at Atlético Madrid.

items.title: AMD's sales jump 45% as demand for AI chips nearly doubles
items.why: The US chipmaker AMD said third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.4 billion, with its data-centre business, which sells AI processors, up 97% to a record $8.5 billion. It expects about $17 billion in sales this quarter, and its shares rose about 8% after hours.
items.matters: It suggests companies are still spending heavily on AI computing, even as investors worry about whether that spending will pay off.

items.title: Catalan writer Cristina Fernández Cubas wins the Cervantes Prize
items.why: Spain's culture minister, Ernest Urtasun, announced on Tuesday that the short-story writer, born in 1945, has won the Spanish-speaking world's top literary award, worth €125,000. The jury praised her originality and her renewal of the contemporary short story. She is the seventh woman to win since 1976.
items.matters: King Felipe VI will present the prize in April at the University of Alcalá de Henares, near Madrid.

items.title: Nordic and other nations refuse to play Russia at ice hockey worlds
items.why: Norway, Denmark and Sweden said they will not play Russia at the 2027 men's world championship in Germany, joining Finland; Latvia's and the Czech federations said the same. The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week that Russia, barred since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, must be readmitted.
items.matters: The sport's governing body, the IIHF, says it is disappointed by the ruling and is working out how to comply.

items.title: Philippe Jaenada wins France's Prix Goncourt for true-crime novel
items.why: The French writer, 62, won France's top literary prize in Paris on Tuesday for 'L'Inconnue du quai de Javel', which reinvestigates the unsolved murder of a young woman found on a Seine quay more than 70 years ago. The Renaudot prize went to François-Henri Désérable for 'Le Palais'.

items.title: EU court adviser says AI chatbots may infringe news publishers' rights
items.why: An adviser to the EU's top court, Advocate General Maciej Szpunar, said chatbots such as Google's Gemini may breach press publishers' rights when they reuse articles' wording or get past paywalls. He said training AI on such material is generally allowed. The case was brought by Hungarian publisher Like Company.
items.matters: The opinion is not binding, but the court usually follows it; a ruling is expected within months.

sources.name: Court of Justice of the EU

items.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies after on-pitch collision
items.why: Jesús de Miguel, a 30-year-old Tenerife forward, died on Tuesday morning, a day after colliding with Andorra's goalkeeper in a Spanish second-division match in the Canary Islands. Police have opened an inquiry, as Spanish law requires, but the local chief prosecutor said criminal proceedings were unlikely.
items.matters: Spain's football federation postponed Tuesday's matches and UEFA ordered a silence before this week's European games.

items.title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia postponed to December 2027
items.why: The Asian Football Confederation has moved the 24-team tournament, due to start in Riyadh on 7 January 2027, to 23 December 2027 to 21 January 2028. It cited travel disruption and logistical problems from regional developments; Yemen's Houthis have claimed drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia.
items.matters: The new dates still need approval from FIFA, football's world governing body.

items.title: Australia's central bank raises interest rates to an 18-year high
items.why: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 0.25 points to 4.85% on Tuesday, its fifth rise this year, in a 6–3 vote. It blamed higher fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict and expects inflation, now 4.3%, to stay high until late 2027.
items.matters: Australia's big four banks are raising variable mortgage rates; ANZ says that adds about A$79 a month to a A$500,000 loan.

items.title: Collins Dictionary names 'mogging' its 2026 word of the year
items.why: Collins, the British dictionary publisher, chose the slang word, meaning outshining or upstaging someone, often playfully. It says use of the word rose 210% in 2026. Other words on its list included 'ghost jobs', for vacancies with no plan to hire, and 'carspreading', for ever-bigger cars.
items.matters: Collins says the word has moved from online forums into everyday speech among younger people.

items.title: Ukraine says Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia aid point killed at least 33
items.why: Guided bombs hit a school used as an aid point in the village of Komyshuvakha, in south-eastern Ukraine, on Monday as residents gathered for aid, Ukrainian officials say. President Zelensky says at least 33 people were killed. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted Ukrainian military units.
items.matters: The US says Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet for new talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November.

items.title: Karl Bushby arrives home in Hull after 28-year walk around the world
items.why: British former paratrooper Karl Bushby reached his mother's house in Hull, northern England, on Monday, ending a walk that began in Punta Arenas, Chile, in November 1998. He covered about 50,000 km through some 30 countries, swimming the Caspian Sea and English Channel rather than use transport.

items.changed: Updated: the suspected attack spread to at least nine European countries, and Belgian prosecutors have opened an investigation.
items.title: Suspected cyberattack disrupts supermarket fridges in nine European countries
items.why: Fridges and freezers failed on Monday at supermarkets in Belgium, Ireland, Sweden, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Finland and Estonia, AFP reports, with Belgium hardest hit. Nobody has claimed responsibility; some affected systems were made by Danish firm Danfoss. Ireland's SuperValu says its 13 stores are back to normal.
items.matters: It follows a similar attack on French supermarkets in October; the EU food commissioner called it a deliberate attack on food supplies.

items.changed: Updated: Brent fell more than 7% on Monday and slipped again on Tuesday, despite a reported US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island.
items.title: Oil prices fall more than 7% on hopes of a US–Iran deal
items.why: Brent crude fell more than 7% on Monday to about $104.77 a barrel as Washington and Tehran signalled openness to talks mediated by Qatar, and slipped again on Tuesday to $103.60. Prices briefly rose after US officials said the US had struck Iran's Qeshm Island.
items.matters: Oil prices feed into fuel, flight and food costs worldwide; Brent ended October at a six-month high.

items.changed: Updated: opposition leaders back Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister as Herzog's consultations begin.
items.title: Israel's opposition backs Eisenkot as Herzog begins coalition talks
items.why: Opposition leaders including Naftali Bennett, Yair Lapid and Avigdor Liberman agreed on Tuesday to recommend Gadi Eisenkot as prime minister. President Isaac Herzog starts consultations on Wednesday. Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 of 120 seats and the Jewish-led opposition 48; Arab-led parties, with 19, are expected to back Eisenkot.
items.matters: Herzog will choose who first tries to form a government; Netanyahu wants a 'broad national government' under him.

items.changed: Updated: owners are reopening factories and the new wage board has started work.
items.title: Bangladesh garment owners move to reopen factories after wage protests
items.why: Clothing makers said they would reopen factories around Dhaka on Tuesday after meeting Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed; industrial police said 414 were still shut on Monday. Workers want a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, up from 12,500. A new government wage board is due to meet this week.
items.matters: The new pay structure must take effect from 1 December; garments are Bangladesh's biggest export.

items.title: Bolivia declares national emergency as El Niño drought hits farming families
items.why: Bolivia's President Rodrigo Paz declared a national emergency on 31 October over drought and other El Niño risks. The defence ministry says at least 114,000 families in six of nine departments have been hit since June, with more than 75,000 cattle lost.
items.matters: Officials warn the coming rainy season could bring floods to other parts of the country while dry areas stay parched.

items.changed: Updated: US strikes on Qeshm Island; Qatar says it still hopes for an interim deal.
items.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Qatar says deal still possible
items.why: US officials say limited 'defensive' strikes hit Iran's Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, on Monday night, saying Iran fired at US aircraft. Qatar, which is carrying proposals between the two sides, says there is still 'hope' of an interim deal.
items.matters: Vice-President JD Vance says there is no deadline for a deal; oil prices fell on hopes of a settlement.

items.changed: Updated: latest health ministry figures (to 1 November) and new US entry rule
items.title: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo pass 5,100
items.why: Congo's health ministry says the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak, declared in May, had killed at least 5,126 people among 10,532 confirmed cases by 1 November. Most cases are in the eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for this strain.
items.matters: Since 3 November the US requires everyone flying in to declare they have not been in Congo in the past 21 days.
